This approach requires changes in the CLIENTE to combine values in a single string and custom parsing logic in the authorizer, and yet does not give the authorizer automatic access to the IP DE ORIGEM (type-authorizers TOKEN receive only 'authorizationToken', 'methodArn' and limited context) — type REQUEST natively provides the full context of the request, including IP of origin, without concatenation in the client.

Incorrect. Authorizers of the type TOKEN only support UMA ONLY identity source, used as a cache key and as the value of 'authorizationToken' passed to the function Lambda; specify multiple sources separated by comma is a capacity of the type REQUEST, Not of a kind TOKEN.

Incorrect. Authorizers COGNITO_USER_POOLS validate JWTs issued by a User Pool of Cognito; they cannot be configured to derive authorization decisions from arbitrary headers and query string parameters that are not part of the claims of the JWT — an authorizer Lambda custom type REQUEST is necessary for this logic customized with multiple sources.

dva-avc-119.text: A microservice emits signed tokens (e.g. custom JWTs) that will be verified by OUTROS The security team demands that the CHAVE PRIVADA OF ASSINATURA NUNCA exit a safe limit / never be exposed to the application code, while other services (or external parts) must achieve VERIFICAR signatures using a CHAVE PUBLIC. What configuration of the KMS meets this requirement?
options: Use a symmetric key of the KMS with operations 'GenerateMac'/ 'VerifyMac'' (HMAC), sharing the symmetric key ID with the checkers so they can call 'VerifyMac''.

Create a SIMETRIC key from KMS and use 'GenerateDataKeyPair' to generate a couple of keys RSA, distributing the serving PRIVADA for the microservice sign and the PUBLIC portion for the verifying parties.
Store a private key RSA generated locally (e.g. via OpenSSL) as a SecureString parameter in Systems Manager Parameter Store, and the microservice recovers and uses this key in memory to sign.

Create a CHAVE ASSIMETRIC OF KMS with key use 'SIGN_VERIFY' (key spec RSA or ECC) — the application calls 'Sign' of KMS (passing message/digest) to produce a signature using key material PRIVADA, that NUNCA exit from KMS; other services/partners may obtain the PUBLIC key (via 'GetPublicKey' or public key distribution) for 'Verify' (locally or via KMS 'Verify') the signatures, without ever needing access to the private key.
dva-avc-119.explanation: Correct. Asymmetric keys to the KMS with use 'SIGN_VERIFY' keep the key material PRIVADA entirely within the KMS — Sign operations are executed internally by KMS. The corresponding PUBLIC key can be exported via 'GetPublicKey' and freely distributed for third party verification without exposing the private key.
dva-avc-119.hint: Think about which configuration of the KMS executes the signature operation internally, without ever returning the private key material to the caller.
optionRationales: Correct. Asymmetric keys to the KMS with use 'SIGN_VERIFY' keep the key material PRIVADA entirely within the KMS — Sign operations are executed internally by KMS. The corresponding PUBLIC key can be exported via 'GetPublicKey' and freely distributed for third party verification without exposing the private key.

Incorrect. 'GenerateDataKeyPair' RETORNA the private key (in clear text and as encrypted blob) to CHAMADOR — i.e., the private key material SAI of the KMS and is exposed to the application code, directly contrary to the requirement. KMS with use 'SIGN_VERIFY' keeps the material private DENTRO of the KMS, performing 'Sign' on the service side.

Incorrect. MACs based on HMAC use one CHAVE SECRETA COMPARTILHADA both to generate and to verify the MAC; sharing this capacity with other services/partners would require that they also have permissions from KMS on the MESMA symmetric key (or the key material itself), which does not correspond to a public/private key verification model, where verifiers need only a PUBLIC key, without access to the key/signing permissions.

Incorrect. This exposes the MATERIAL DA CHAVE PRIVADA to the application memory/runtime (even if encrypted at rest in the Parameter Store, it is described and made available to the application process during signature) — directly contrary to the requirement that the private key never be exposed to the application code; asymmetric keys KMS with 'SIGN_VERIFY' perform the signature without ever exposing the private key.

dva-avc-120.text: A function Lambda is configured to run within SUBNETS PRIVADAS of a VPC (no NAT Gateway, no route to Internet Gateway) for compliance reasons — it has no route to the public internet. The function needs to call 'GetSecretValue' Secrets Manager to obtain database credentials in runtime. Without internet access, the call to 'secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com' failure/expire. How to allow this access while keeping the function traffic out of the public internet?
options: Create a INTERFACE VPC ENDPOINT (AWS PrivateLink) for the Secrets Manager ('com.amazonaws.<region>.secretsmanager') the VPC, associated with route tables/security groups private subnets — this provides ENIs with private IP addresses in VPC that solve 'secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com' via integration with private host area of Route 53, allowing the function Lambda (on the private subnet, attached to VPC) scope or Secrets Manager via PrivateLink without crossing the public internet or requiring a NAT Gateway.
Configure a GATEWAY VPC ENDPOINT for the Secrets Manager and add a route to it in the private subnet route table, in the same pattern used for S3 and DynamoDB.
Add one NAT Gateway on a public subnet and set up the private subnet route table to send traffic '0.0.0.0/0' through it, allowing access to the internet exit for the call to Secrets Manager.
Remove function Lambda of VPC, as it functions Lambda not attached to a VPC have direct access to service endpoints of the AWS, including the Secrets Manager, by the internal network of the AWS.
dva-avc-120.explanation: Right. VPC Endpoint for 'com.amazonaws.<region>.secretsmanager' provides ENIs with private IPs within the VPC and, with the integration of DNS private enabled, makes calls to the default endpoint of Secrets Manager are resolved for these private IPs — allowing access to Secrets Manager entirely within the network of the VPC/AWS, without public internet NAT Gateway.
dva-avc-120.hint: Think of what kind of VPC Endpoint or Secrets Manager supports, and if this type provides network interfaces with private IP or only adds an entry in the route table.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Endpoint for 'com.amazonaws.<region>.secretsmanager' provides ENIs with private IPs within the VPC and, with the integration of DNS private enabled, makes calls to the default endpoint of Secrets Manager are resolved for these private IPs — allowing access to Secrets Manager entirely within the network of the VPC/AWS, without public internet NAT Gateway.

Incorrect. Although it's true that it works Lambda FORA of a VPC achieve the Secrets Manager directly, the scenario requires the function to remain DENTRO of the private subnets of the VPC for reasons of COMPLIANCE (for example, to also access a database RDS in the same VPC) — remove it from VPC is not an option; an Interface VPC Endpoint allows resources attached to VPC reach or Secrets Manager in private.

Incorrect. Secrets Manager I can't stand it. GATEWAY VPC Endpoints — only Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB support this type; or Secrets Manager (as most of the other services of AWS) requires a INTERFACE VPC Endpoint (based on ENI, via PrivateLink).

Incorrect. NAT Gateway PERMITISSE if the call were successful (providing Internet access), traffic would pass through INTERNET PUBLIC (see the public IP of NAT Gateway) to reach the public endpoint of Secrets Manager, which may violate the compliance requirement to keep traffic off the public internet — an Interface VPC Endpoint keeps traffic entirely within the network of AWS/VPC.
